children.name: Project title
children.text: LUMBOX: B2B Platform for Indonesia’s Agricultural Supply Chain

children.name: Project description
children.text: Designing an integrated platform for aggregators, smallholder farmers, buyers, and ID FOOD's staff and executives, connecting every layer of Indonesia's agricultural supply chain in one system.

children.name: Type value
children.text: Case Submission for Prototype Design Competition (International Level)

children.name: Team value
children.text:
Nadya Euvania 
(UX Researcher)
Abdul Aziz Zaki Hidayat
(UI/UX Designer)

children.name: Overview text
children.text: Every year, Indonesia loses enough food to feed 125 million people, while farmers capture only a fraction of what it's worth.

children.name: Overview text
children.text: Lumbox is our submission for Proto-A-Thon International Design Competition 2026, developed for a case study in collaboration with ID FOOD, Indonesia's state-owned food holding company. Here's the problem we uncovered, and the system we designed to solve it.

children.name: Problem description
children.text: Indonesia's food supply chain loses IDR 551 trillion annually (4-5% of GDP) to inefficiency. Prices markup 7-10x from farmer to consumer, yet farmers capture just 15-20% of that value, leaving 48 million smallholder farmers excluded from formal markets and fair pricing.

children.name: Solution description
children.text: A platform that formalizes, not eliminates, the informal actors already holding the chain together (tengkulak). Connecting 500,000+ aggregators and 48 million smallholder farmers to verified B2B buyers, tailored across every level of the organization, from field collectors to ID FOOD's staff and executives.

children.name: Problem description
children.text: To understand why the system was breaking, we started by mapping where the money and the food were actually going.

children.name: Metric 1 description
children.text: Lost annually 4–5% of GDP, exceeding the entire Ministry of Agriculture budget.

children.name: Metric 2 description
children.text: Average distribution time for fresh produce, against a 1–3 day shelf life.

children.name: Metric 3 description
children.text: Price markup from farmer to consumer while farmers capture only 15–20%.

children.name: Metric 4 description
children.text: Smallholder farmers still excluded from formal markets and digital systems.

children.name: Problem summary
children.text: The crisis is not a lack of harvest, capital, or ambition, it is the absence of a unifying layer that connects what already exists

children.name: Goals text
children.text: The future of Indonesia’s food supply chain is not built by removing intermediaries entirely, but by formalizing and orchestrating their essential functions into a transparent, tech-enabled ecosystem

children.name: Goals text
children.text: Here’s what we’re committing to build:

children.name: Goals summary
children.text: Rather than disrupting the actors already holding this chain together (informal aggregators/tengkulak), we set out to formalize and orchestrate them, building a system where every role becomes more valuable, not obsolete.

children.name: HMW intro text
children.text: After interviewing farmers and middlemen across the supply chain and analyzing where the system breaks down, we distilled everything into one core question:

children.name: HMW question text
children.text: “How might we create a more transparent, connected, and efficient food supply chain ecosystem that helps farmers, middlemen, and businesses access fair pricing, smarter distribution, reliable logistics, and data-driven decision making while reducing food waste and market uncertainty?”

children.name: Solution intro
children.text: With that question in mind, we looked at why past agritech solutions had failed and realized most of them tried to eliminate the very actors, like tengkulak (middlemen), who were quietly holding the chain together. So instead of removing them, we designed a system to formalize what they already do.

children.name: Products description
children.text: Three surfaces. One ecosystem. Every actor in chain, from the farmer who grows it, to the collector who moves it, to the business that needs it, finally connected

children.name: Product 1 description

children.name: Feature 1 title
children.text: TRANSPARENT FARM PRODUCTS COLLECTION & CONNECTIVITY THROUGH LUMBOX CONNECT

children.name: Feature 1 description
children.text: The collector negotiates with the farmer on-site and inputs the transaction details into the app: Farmer’s Name/NIK, Commodity, Volume, Agreed Price/kg, and Payment Method (Cash or Cashless via Bank Account). To finalize the purchase, the collector must trigger an automated summary sent directly to the farmer’s WhatsApp/SMS. This forces a transparent, honest ledger where the offered price is benchmarked against real-time market data.

Conclusion text
children.text: By activating ID FOOD's existing infrastructure, Lumbox aims to transform informal networks into a connected digital ecosystem, shifting national food governance from reactive monitoring to real-time orchestration.

children.name: Conclusion summary
children.text: From scatterd harvest to a connected nation, built chain by GRAIN.
